verifiedRecords.output: An explicit list of matching edges; its total weight can also be reported.
verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected simple graph; arbitrary finite nonnegative edge weights; n vertices and m edges.
verifiedRecords.oracle: WeightedNeighbor(v,i) returns the i-th neighbor together with its edge weight, or ⊥ past the end of the fixed list. The n labeled vertices are known. No free edge list or global weight table.
verifiedRecords.theorem: Edmonds, Theorems (P), (M), and §7; exact query accounting is an atlas composition.
verifiedRecords.probability: Deterministic exact scan and deterministic exact optimization on the stored graph.
verifiedRecords.notes: Read each vertex list until the first ⊥. There are 2m successful weighted-neighbor replies and n terminal replies, hence exactly n+2m queries. Deduplicate the two copies of each edge and solve the stored weighted graph. Query cost is not computation time.
verifiedRecords.derivation: Read each vertex list until the first ⊥. There are 2m successful weighted-neighbor replies and n terminal replies, hence exactly n+2m queries. Deduplicate the two copies of each edge and solve the stored weighted graph.
verifiedRecords.computation: Run an exact weighted-matching algorithm only after the scan; no further oracle calls. Polynomial-time optimization is separate from the displayed query count.

verifiedRecords.quality: OPT ≤ estimate ≤ OPT+εn, with probability at least 2/3. This is additive error, not a fixed multiplicative ratio.

verifiedRecords.oracle: WeightedNeighbor(v,i) returns the i-th neighbor together with its edge weight, or ⊥ past the end of the fixed list. The n labeled vertices are known. No free edge list or global weight table.

derivedBounds.title: Hidden heavy edge: explicit-output query obstruction
derivedBounds.quality: Any fixed retained fraction β∈(0,1] of optimal matching weight, including exact output.
derivedBounds.output: An explicit β-approximate matching. The lower bound shown is not for an additive scalar estimate.
derivedBounds.graph: Complete graph K_n with all weights 1 except one hidden edge of weight ceil(n/β). Even the entire topology may be supplied for free.
derivedBounds.oracle: WeightedNeighbor(v,i) returns the i-th neighbor together with its edge weight, or ⊥ past the end of the fixed list. The n labeled vertices are known. No free edge list or global weight table.
derivedBounds.theorem: Elementary hidden-heavy-edge proof by the atlas; no separate paper theorem is attributed.
derivedBounds.probability: Any randomized algorithm succeeding with probability at least 2/3 on every input, with a worst-case query budget.
derivedBounds.proof: Let N=n(n−1)/2. Give the algorithm the entire topology of K_n for free. Choose a uniform hidden edge e*, assign it weight H=ceil(n/β), and give every other edge weight 1, for a fixed 0<β≤1. A matching omitting e* has weight at most floor(n/2), while β·OPT≥βH≥n, so every successful β-approximate matching must contain e*. Fix the algorithm’s random coins. Until it reads e*, its transcript is identical to the all-unit-weight graph. Its at-most-q probes inspect at most q distinct edges along that transcript; its no-hit output contains at most floor(n/2) further candidate edges. Thus success over the uniform hidden edge is at most (q+floor(n/2))/N. Averaging over the coins preserves this bound. Success probability at least 2/3 on every input requires q≥2N/3−floor(n/2)=Ω(n²). A weighted-neighbor query or pair query reveals at most one edge weight; duplicated reads do not help. This is a worst-case query-budget bound for explicit matching output, with polynomial weight range H=O(n) when β is fixed. It does not assert a lower bound for εn-additive scalar estimation.
